column2: The Lord addresses Moses, with Eleazar added across the next verse boundary. The sentence remains deliberately incomplete here.
Eleazar is a direct addressee in the selected text. Bronze pans and this strange fire remain explicit; the consecrating clause continues into verse 3.
The sinners' pans become hammered altar-covering plates because they were presented and made holy. At the cost of their lives is the provisional contextual rendering of the life phrase.
column3: The exact relation of sinners and in their lives needs fuller syntactic review.

column2: Eleazar takes the bronze pans, then plural they apply the covering. The shift of agent number remains rather than assigning all work to Eleazar alone.
The memorial excludes non-Aaronic outsiders from incense and warns against Korah's fate. Through Moses retains divine mediation.
Next-day grumbling accuses Moses and Aaron of killing the Lord's people. The accusation remains the speakers' claim.
The congregation gathers against the leaders and rushes toward the tent, followed by cloud covering and visible glory.
Moses and Aaron come before the tent. Area is an English spatial completion, not a named architectural enclosure.
The selected speech addresses both Moses and Aaron.
Withdrawal precedes threatened immediate consumption, and both leaders fall face down. All at once remains temporal idiom.
Aaron takes altar fire and incense quickly into camp for atonement; wrath has already begun striking the people.
Aaron runs into the assembly, where the outbreak has begun, adds incense and makes atonement. The rapid action and sequence remain.
Aaron stands between dead and living, and the outbreak subsides. The spatial contrast is explicit.
The death toll is 14,700, expressly excluding the Korah deaths.
Aaron returns to Moses at the tent entrance; the repeated subsiding statement remains.
A new divine speech introduces the staff test.
Twelve staffs are collected by ancestral houses from leaders, each inscribed with its owner's name. The number and individual inscriptions remain.
Aaron's name goes on Levi's staff; one staff represents each ancestral tribe.
The staffs are placed opposite the testimony inside the tent, at the place of divine self-disclosure.
The chosen man's staff sprouts; removal of grumbling from God is linked to the complaints directed at the human leaders.
The twelve staffs and Aaron's staff among them are both stated without adding an unexpressed thirteenth count.
Moses places the staffs before the Lord in the tent.
Both Moses and Aaron enter next day in the selected text. Shoot, flowers and nuts remain distinct, without replacing the generic nuts by almonds.
All staffs are shown to all Israel, and each man takes his own staff. Both universal expressions remain.
Aaron's staff is preserved before the plural testimonies as a sign for sons of the disobedient. The ending emphatically promises non-death as grumbling ceases.
Both Moses and Aaron obey; the command was given to Moses. These distinct roles remain.
Israel's three parallel cries of consumption and loss remain rather than being reduced to one.
The selected claim concerns touching the tent, followed by a fear of dying to the end; approaching alone is not substituted.
column3: The final question's natural English force needs a further spoken-stage review.

column2: Aaron's paternal house shares responsibility for holy things, while Aaron and sons bear priesthood responsibility. The two scopes are not collapsed.
Levitical brothers join and minister to Aaron; Aaron and sons remain before the tent. The family and tribal descriptions remain.
Levites guard Aaron's and tent charges but may not approach holy vessels or altar. The restriction prevents death for both them and the priests.
Levitical attachment includes all tent ministries; outsiders may not approach Aaron. The recipient is not changed to the tent.
Guarding holy things and altar prevents wrath among Israel. No again is inserted where the selected text does not state it.
The Levites are a gift given to the Lord for tent service. The selected recipient is retained without adding given to you.
Priesthood encompasses altar matters and within the veil, with ministry as its gift. Approaching outsiders face death.
Charge of firstfruits and a share of honour from consecrated things belong to Aaron and his sons after him. Honour is retained for the selected reward term.
Gifts, sacrifices, guilt offerings and sin offerings all supply the holy portions. Their full repeated scope remains.
The selected in-the-holy-of-holies expression is rendered most holy place, with male consumption specified as Aaron and sons.
column3: The locative force and ritual interpretation need specialist review; no harmonizing location is substituted.

column2: This separate class of presentations includes daughters and all clean household members, unlike the preceding male-only clause.
Oil, wine and grain firstfruits are all given to Aaron. The repeated firstfruit vocabulary remains.
All first produce brought to the Lord belongs to Aaron and can be eaten by clean household members.
Everything devoted in Israel belongs to Aaron. No additional devoted category is supplied.
Womb-opening firstborn of humans and livestock belong to Aaron, with mandatory human redemption and redemption of unclean livestock.
Redemption begins at one month, valued at five sanctuary shekels. The parenthetical twenty-obol equivalence refers to the shekel.
Calf, sheep and goat firstborn are not redeemed; blood goes against the altar and fat is offered. All three categories remain.
The flesh belongs to Aaron like the presentation breast and right foreleg. Right remains explicit.
The portion includes sons and daughters under an enduring ordinance. The selected everlasting salt covenant wording remains without explanatory symbolism.
Aaron receives no land portion because God is his portion and inheritance among Israel. Both negative land statements remain.
Every tithe is Levi's allotment in return for tent ministry. The service is the stated basis, not an inferred purchase.
Israel may no longer approach the tent to incur death-bringing sin; the prohibition and consequence remain linked.
The individual Levite's service shifts to plural bearing of offences. Enduring ordinance and no inheritance remain.
column3: The referent of their offences deserves fuller discourse review before an explicit substitution.

column2: Israel's tithes given to the Lord supply Levi's allotment and explain the absence of a separate inheritance among Israel.
The Lord addresses Moses for the further Levitical instruction.
The Levites give a tithe of the received tithe to the Lord. The nested fraction is retained without an added numerical calculation in the verse.
Their contribution is reckoned like threshing-floor grain and a winepress portion, preserving both agricultural comparisons.
Contributions from all tithes go to the Lord through Aaron the priest. Both recipient levels remain.
The selected or links gifts and firstfruits in the contribution instruction; it is not silently changed to and.
column3: The compressed alternative construction needs syntax and apparatus review.

column2: After removing firstfruits, the remainder is reckoned as threshing-floor and winepress produce for Levites. The English it remains implicit rather than naming a different object.
Levites and households may eat in every place, because the food is their wage for tent ministry.
Taking firstfruits prevents guilt; profaning Israel's holy things is forbidden lest they die. Both conditions remain explicit.
